candidates.summary: Pkg.Draft is parsed from gnomod.toml and never read, so the draft half of modFlags is dead
candidates.failure_scenario: LoadPkgs sets pkg.Draft at plan.go:142 and the field is read nowhere: BuildPlan gates on Ignore at plan.go:220 and plan.go:241 and on nothing else, Pkg carries no json tags and is not embedded in Plan. A PR touching examples/gno.land/r/demo/draftrealm (the tree's only draft = true package) is planned, rendered and screenshotted exactly as a non-draft realm, and a reader of the struct is told a filter exists that does not. Either the field and the draft=true case in modFlags (plan.go:161) go, or draft realms are filtered like ignored ones.
candidates.verify_by: grep -rn 'Draft' misc/gnopreview/ -- five hits: plan.go:58 decl, plan.go:142 assign, and nothing else; no read site anywhere in the module
candidates.evidence: grep -rn "Draft\|Ignore" misc/gnopreview/ returned plan.go:58 (decl), plan.go:59 (decl), plan.go:142 (assign both), plan.go:220 (!p.Ignore), plan.go:241 (pkgs[p].Ignore). Draft has no read site. examples/gno.land/r/demo/draftrealm/gnomod.toml is the only file under examples/gno.land carrying draft or ignore.

candidates.summary: the plan step pipes the new binary into tee, so a non-zero exit is discarded and the skip gate reads an empty plan.json
candidates.failure_scenario: pr-preview.yml sets no shell: key and no defaults:, so GitHub runs the step as bash -e {0} with no pipefail. In `"$RUNNER_TEMP/gnopreview" plan -changed changed.txt | tee plan.json` the pipeline's status is tee's, so any failure of the just-built binary (root discovery per main.go:300, an unreadable changed.txt, a WalkDir error in LoadPkgs) leaves plan.json empty and the step green. jq then reads the empty file, prints nothing and exits 0, so the comparison against "no" fails, skip stays unset, and the job goes on to build gnodev and check out the merge base before render hits the same error. The reader gets a red preview job pointing at render, minutes after the step that actually failed.
candidates.verify_by: grep -n 'shell:|defaults:|pipefail|set -e' .github/workflows/pr-preview.yml returns nothing; then bash -e -c 'false | tee x; echo rc=$?' prints rc=0 and continues, and jq -r 'if .gnoweb or (.realms | length > 0) then "yes" else "no" end' on an empty file prints nothing with rc=0
candidates.evidence: grep for shell:/defaults:/pipefail/set -e in pr-preview.yml: no matches. `bash -e -c 'false | tee x.json; echo "after pipe, rc=$?"; echo reached-next-line'` printed "after pipe, rc=0" then "reached-next-line"; the same under -eo pipefail exited 1. jq on an empty plan.json: stdout=[] rc=0, so the gate does not skip.

candidates.summary: gnoweb seed realms are appended after the maxRealms truncation, so the rendered count exceeds the cap while Dropped reports the pre-seed number
candidates.failure_scenario: BuildPlan truncates realms to maxRealms and records plan.Dropped at plan.go:256-258, and only then, at plan.go:262, appends every gnowebSeedRealms entry not already present. A PR that touches gnoweb and more than maxRealms realms renders up to maxRealms+4 realms, each with its own gnodev crawl and screenshots, past the bound the flag names; the comment built from plan.Dropped tells the reader N were dropped while the list under it is longer than the cap. The seeds also skip the Realm and Ignore filters applied at plan.go:241. Seeding before the sort and the cap fixes both.
candidates.verify_by: read plan.go:250-270 for the order of truncation and seeding; build a Plan with maxRealms=2, three changed realms and a gnoweb change, and count len(plan.Realms) against maxRealms
candidates.evidence: plan.go:256 `if maxRealms > 0 && len(realms) > maxRealms { plan.Dropped = len(realms) - maxRealms; realms = realms[:maxRealms] }` then plan.go:261-268 `if plan.Gnoweb { for _, r := range gnowebSeedRealms { if pkgs[r] != nil && !contains(plan.Realms, r) { plan.Realms = append(plan.Realms, r) } } }`. gnowebSeedRealms holds 4 entries.

candidates.summary: the module requires nothing, so plan.go carries a second gnomod.toml reader beside gnovm/pkg/gnomod and accepts only one spelling of the flags
candidates.failure_scenario: go.mod declares no dependency on github.com/gnolang/gno, so the planner cannot call the repo's own parser for the file it reads. modFlags (plan.go:155-167) instead scans lines and compares strings.ReplaceAll(strings.TrimSpace(line), " ", "") against the literals "draft=true" and "ignore=true". Valid TOML that gnomod.ParseBytes reads and this misses: a trailing comment (`ignore = true # quarantined`), a tab between the key and the value, and a key under any table rather than the top level. An ignored package then re-enters the plan at plan.go:220 and plan.go:241, gnodev is asked to load a package the gno toolchain ignores, and the reviewer gets a preview page for a realm that does not exist on chain. Latent at this head: examples/gno.land/r/demo/draftrealm/gnomod.toml is the only flagged file under the walked root and it uses the plain form. The tradeoff is the maintainer's: a require plus replace on the root module buys gnovm/pkg/gnomod and costs the dependency-free build the workflows rely on.
candidates.verify_by: cat -A examples/gno.land/r/demo/draftrealm/gnomod.toml for the live spelling, then feed modFlags a file whose line is `ignore = true # why` and compare its result with gnomod.ParseBytes on the same bytes
candidates.evidence: go.mod is three lines, module + go 1.25.9, no require block and no go.sum; `GOPROXY=off go test ./...` passes offline, confirming zero non-stdlib deps. gnovm/pkg/gnomod/file.go:21,27 declare Ignore and Draft with toml tags and gnovm/pkg/gnomod/parse.go exports ParseBytes/ParseFilepath. cat -A of the one live flagged file shows `draft = true$`, the spelling modFlags handles.
